beats.text: You know the pause after you finish talking to an AI? Three labs erased it this week, one reply lands in 450 milliseconds.
beats.show_cue: Operator on camera holding a real walkie talkie, then swapping it for a phone mid sentence.
curiosity_queries: SeedRealtime full duplex voice AI clip
walkie talkie versus phone call stock footage

beats.text: Nvidia's new voice model answers in about 450 milliseconds, fast enough to check something mid sentence without losing the thread. The same team also open sourced voices in twelve languages. Both are downloads, not subscriptions.
beats.show_cue: The Nvidia model card held on the 450 millisecond turn-taking line, then the Magpie TTS languages list.
curiosity_queries: Nvidia Magpie TTS multilingual voice agent demo
450 millisecond voice AI turn taking sample

beats.text: Then MiniMax shipped a model that makes video with the sound already inside it, nothing bolted on after. Old voice AI is a walkie talkie: talk, wait, talk. This is a phone call, both sides can jump in.
beats.show_cue: MiniMax's own generated sample clip with native audio, then the GitHub repo page.
curiosity_queries: MiniMax H3 video audio generation sample

beats.text: Every number here is the lab's own, nobody outside has run these live yet. The open model is licensed for research only, and a live call holds a whole GPU open the entire time. Worth trying this week, not on your phone lines yet.
beats.show_cue: The model card's research only licence line, then a live nvidia-smi terminal readout for the GPU cost.
